prompt:
IMAGE TASK: CREATE CANONICAL SCENE ANCHOR
Asset: A1 | Scene: S1
Reference assets: A0
Reference views: rear_left_45, rear
SUBJECT IDENTITY LOCK
A dark charcoal/black freestanding two-door top-freezer refrigerator matching the approved A0 canonical multi-view reference pack: rectangular body, upper freezer door smaller than lower refrigerator door, thin silver horizontal divider/trim between doors, minimal recessed vertical black handles along the left edge, flat dark side panels, compact household proportions.
Must preserve:
- dark charcoal/black body color
- top-freezer two-door layout
- upper freezer door smaller than lower refrigerator door
- thin silver horizontal divider between doors
- recessed vertical handle geometry on the left side
- same height-to-width proportions as the product reference
- same flat-sided rectangular body design
Must never change:
- do not convert to French-door, side-by-side, single-door, or bottom-freezer layout
- do not change body color to white or stainless steel
- do not add external water/ice dispenser
- do not add large protruding handles
- do not change door proportions
- do not invent a different appliance model
SCENE INTENT
Narration: Vì sao phía sau tủ lạnh lại nóng, trong khi bên trong thì lạnh?
Visual goal: Establish the exact refrigerator from the product reference inside a real kitchen, with a clear rear three-quarter view that makes the back/side area visually accessible for later explanation.
Viewer should understand:
- this is one specific household refrigerator that will remain the same throughout the video
- the video is about the warm rear/heat-rejection area
- the scene is observational, before any technical overlay appears
CAMERA
View: Rear three-quarter view of the same refrigerator, showing approximately 55–65% of the rear plane and 35–45% of one side/front edge; front doors may be only partially visible as identity cues.
Angle: Camera positioned behind and slightly to the left of the refrigerator, about 35–45 degrees off the rear normal.
Distance: Medium full-body shot with the entire refrigerator visible from feet to top.
Height: Camera center around mid-door height, approximately 1.2–1.4 m from floor.
Framing: Vertical 9:16; refrigerator occupies about 65–75% of image height, with clear margins around rear edges.
Perspective: Natural household-camera perspective with vertical lines kept straight.
Lens style: Moderate 35–50 mm equivalent; avoid ultra-wide distortion.
COMPOSITION
Subject position: Refrigerator centered slightly left so the rear panel is unobstructed and readable.
Background visibility: Kitchen background visible but secondary; no object may overlap the rear panel.
Negative space: Leave useful clear space to the right/rear side for later arrows or labels.
Crop rules:
- do not crop feet, top edge, rear panel, or silver door divider
- keep enough floor and wall context to establish a real kitchen
- rear panel must not be hidden against the wall
Layering:
- foreground: none
- midground: refrigerator
- background: stable kitchen
ENVIRONMENT
Location: Ordinary modern home kitchen with enough clearance around the refrigerator to view its side/rear area.
Fixed elements:
- warm light-wood cabinetry
- light neutral wall
- simple light-colored tile or wood-look floor
- one small green plant or modest kitchen accessory
- no people
Allowed changes:
- small crop adjustments
- subtle camera repositioning required by each scene
- minor background blur consistent with the same kitchen
Forbidden changes:
- no showroom or appliance-store setting
- no industrial kitchen
- no dramatic location change
- no neon or sci-fi environment
- no unrelated refrigerator in the background
LIGHTING
Style: Natural residential daylight with soft practical kitchen fill.
Direction: Main daylight from camera-right/front-right; soft fill from room lighting.
Intensity: Moderate, realistic indoor exposure; refrigerator surfaces remain dark but readable.
Color temperature: Neutral-warm daylight, approximately household natural-light appearance.
Consistency rules:
- keep shadow direction consistent across A1/A2/A5/A6
- avoid dramatic rim light or studio spotlight
- do not make the refrigerator glossy or mirror-like
MATERIALS AND REALISM
Materials:
- matte or satin dark-coated metal refrigerator exterior
- thin brushed-metal/silver divider trim
- ordinary painted kitchen walls
- wood cabinetry
- realistic floor material
Surface finish:
- subtle real-world texture
- small natural reflections only
- no perfect CGI plastic smoothness
Reality notes:
- ordinary lived-in kitchen, not a product advertisement set
- physically plausible contact shadows and floor reflections
- straight edges remain geometrically consistent
- no melted, duplicated, or warped appliance parts
REQUIRED VISUAL ELEMENTS
1. the exact dark two-door top-freezer refrigerator identity
   Placement: center-left, full body
   State: closed doors, normal operation, no overlays
   Purpose: canonical identity anchor
2. rear exterior plane
   Placement: clearly visible behind the refrigerator body
   State: plain realistic rear casing; no invented exposed coil network unless directly supported by reference
   Purpose: establish the area discussed by the hook
3. small realistic wall clearance
   Placement: between rear of refrigerator and wall
   State: enough to visually read the rear area
   Purpose: make heat-rejection area physically plausible
TECHNICAL OVERLAY
- none
ALLOWED TRANSFORMS
- select and faithfully reconstruct the approved A0 rear-left-45/rear geometry into the vertical scene composition
- place the unchanged canonical refrigerator into the defined kitchen environment
TECHNICAL CONSTRAINTS
- A0 defines product geometry; do not invent an alternate rear shape or door proportion.
- Do not expose or invent compressor, condenser coil, tubing or internal refrigeration components in A1.
- A1 is an observational scene anchor only; technical mechanism is introduced later.
CONTINUITY CONSTRAINTS
- A0 is the canonical geometry and identity source for fridge_01.
- A1 becomes the scene-composition anchor for later physical scenes.
- Later A2/A5/A6 must preserve A0 geometry and A1 kitchen/lighting continuity.
NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS
- no white refrigerator
- no stainless-steel refrigerator
- no different door layout
- no product showroom
- no excessive blur
- no people
- no open doors
- no glowing heat effect
- no arrows or labels
- no exposed invented technical internals
OUTPUT
1080x1920, aspect ratio 9:16
Opaque background.
FINAL RULE
A0 is the canonical geometry source. Build this scene from the requested A0 view(s) without redesigning the product.
